page: Microsoft Azure F1amds_v7 is an entry-level compute-optimized virtual machine provisioned on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. The instance is powered by a dedicated single physical core and single vCPU from the AMD EPYC 9V45 processor line, operating at up to 4.5 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. Hardware features include 48 KB L1 data cache, 1.0 MB L2 cache, and a substantial 32 MB L3 cache slice. Supported instruction sets include AVX-512 extensions (AVX-512F, AVX-512 VNNI, and BF16) along with standard vector extensions, hardware-accelerated cryptography via AES, VAES, and SHA-NI, as well as SVM virtualization. The server is equipped with 8.0 GB of memory and includes a 118 GB local NVMe solid-state drive.

Benchmark results demonstrate exceptional single-thread processing capabilities, driven by high core clock rates and advanced vector execution. The instance achieves top-decile performance in stress-ng single-core execution alongside top-tier throughput in single-threaded compression tests, registering 40.97 GB/s in gzip compression and 18.14 GB/s in bzip3 decompression. Uncached memory bandwidth performs in the median tier, delivering 41.25 GB/s read and 31.95 GB/s write speeds across large memory blocks. However, total system throughput is constrained by the single-core topology, resulting in bottom-quartile marks in multi-threaded PassMark CPU metrics, Redis SET operations, and static web serving throughput.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the F1amds_v7 offers a high-frequency dedicated core paired with bundled NVMe storage and an above-average memory-to-core ratio of 8 GB per vCPU, avoiding the CPU contention common to burstable tiers. The principal engineering tradeoff lies in total multi-threaded scalability and aggregate networking limits. The instance is suited for single-threaded batch processing, lightweight microservices, build steps, data compression pipelines, and small memory-resident tasks requiring fast local scratch storage.
description: Microsoft Azure F1amds_v7 is a single-core compute-optimized virtual machine running on an AMD EPYC 9V45 processor clocked at up to 4.5 GHz. It provides 1 dedicated vCPU, 8.0 GB of system memory, and a bundled 118 GB local NVMe SSD. Single-threaded performance benchmarks place the instance in the top decile for CPU stress testing and data compression tasks, supported by hardware AVX-512 and cryptographic instruction sets. However, the single-core configuration inherently limits overall multi-core throughput, database transaction volume, and concurrent web serving capacity. With a balanced 8 GB allocation per vCPU and fast local storage, the instance delivers a stable execution profile for lightweight utilities, single-threaded processing scripts, edge microservices, and small-scale batch workloads.
